akhfash:11-11.t:
And He said ﴿لاَغِيَةً﴾, that is: you will not hear a word of idle talk (لغو), and He made it ﴿لاَغِيَةً﴾. The proof for this is that you say "فارِس" for the owner of a horse (فَرَس), "دارِع" for the owner of a coat of mail (دِرْع), and "شاعر" for the possessor of poetry (شِعْر). And the poet said [in the majzūʾ al-kāmil metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-eighth verse cited as evidence]:
* أَغررتَنِي وَزَعَمْتَ أَنَّكَ لابِنٌ بِالصَّيْفِ تامِرْ *
(Did you deceive me, claiming that in summer you are a man of milk and a man of dates?)
That is: an owner of milk and an owner of dates. «[Translator's note: the source gives this verse the same number as the verse cited at 81:4.]»
